Request For Proposal 168884 JA-207652 Student and Staff Computing Devices

SCOPE AND SPECIFICATIONS OF THE
PROPOSAL
requirements to procure vendors who provide goods or services purchased by Dallas ISD using federal
dollars. This proposal may be used with local, state, federal, and grant-funded programs.
PURPOSE OF REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)
This Request for Proposal (RFP) will be for student and staff computing devices, including laptops,
desktops, tablet devices, and display monitors. Vendors participating in this Request for Proposal (RFP) may
submit proposals for one, several, or all categories of devices required by the District. Within each category
of device, the District reserves the right to award contracts to a single vendor or multiple vendors.

Return exactly one JSON entry per requested field,
using only retrieved evidence. Each entry has name, value, source_chunk_ids,
confidence and notes. Values are text or null. A non-null value requires exact
retrieved chunk IDs. Missing fields use null, [], 0 and notes='Not found in
retrieved evidence'. Missing retrieval does not prove absence from the documents.
Explicit negative requirements may be reported as text; absence alone is not 'No'.
Confidence is an uncalibrated evidence-support estimate, not search similarity.
When sources give different values for the same field, cite all supporting chunks
and explain both values with their source file and page/section in notes.
If an addendum explicitly changes that field and its order is established, use
the latest valid updated value in value and explain the original value and change
in notes. An explicit statement that an addendum changes the deadline establishes
precedence over a differing portal listing; a timezone discrepancy does not undo
that explicit change. Preserve the addendum's written time zone without conversion.
Unrelated addendums do not override the field. Search rank or similarity
does not establish precedence. Do not invent an earlier value absent from evidence.
If precedence is unclear, use value=null, cite the conflicting evidence, set
confidence=0, and explain both values and the unresolved conflict in notes.
Null with citations means unresolved conflict; null without citations means missing.
Preserve stated dates, time zones and relative windows; do not invent details.
A bidder question is not an official requirement: use the official Answer when present.
Never infer "not required" from equipment having an operating system already installed.
Preserve who each rule applies to: district, prime vendor, subcontractor or supplier.
Multiple permitted options or cooperative arrangements are not conflicting values;
list all supported options and explain whether participation is optional.
Keep device categories separate. Do not transfer specifications from one category to another.
Use a heading_context only to identify a passage's category; it supplies no missing specifications.
Do not assume a warranty, operating system, quantity or other unstated value.
For broad fields, enumerate all categories supported by the supplied evidence and
explicitly identify incomplete coverage. Do not turn a subset into an all-devices claim.
If a fixed delivery date is absent but scheduling or a relative window is supported,
report that information and say the fixed date is not established.
Table evidence with table_complete=false is partial; do not claim a complete list.

Requested fields:
- Bid Number: Official solicitation / RFP identifier.
- Title: Full title of the bid or RFP.
- Due Date: Submission deadline with stated time zone. An explicitly revised deadline in the latest numbered addendum overrides a differing portal listing: use its stated deadline verbatim and describe the portal discrepancy in notes. Do not leave it unresolved merely because the portal shows another time.

Return exactly one JSON entry per requested field,
using only retrieved evidence. Each entry has name, value, source_chunk_ids,
confidence and notes. Values are text or null. A non-null value requires exact
retrieved chunk IDs. Missing fields use null, [], 0 and notes='Not found in
retrieved evidence'. Missing retrieval does not prove absence from the documents.
Explicit negative requirements may be reported as text; absence alone is not 'No'.
Confidence is an uncalibrated evidence-support estimate, not search similarity.
When sources give different values for the same field, cite all supporting chunks
and explain both values with their source file and page/section in notes.
If an addendum explicitly changes that field and its order is established, use
the latest valid updated value in value and explain the original value and change
in notes. An explicit statement that an addendum changes the deadline establishes
precedence over a differing portal listing; a timezone discrepancy does not undo
that explicit change. Preserve the addendum's written time zone without conversion.
Unrelated addendums do not override the field. Search rank or similarity
does not establish precedence. Do not invent an earlier value absent from evidence.

confidence=0, and explain both values and the unresolved conflict in notes.

input.content:
Return exactly one JSON entry per requested field,
using only retrieved evidence. Each entry has name, value, source_chunk_ids,
confidence and notes. Values are text or null. A non-null value requires exact
retrieved chunk IDs. Missing fields use null, [], 0 and notes='Not found in
retrieved evidence'. Missing retrieval does not prove absence from the documents.
Explicit negative requirements may be reported as text; absence alone is not 'No'.
Confidence is an uncalibrated evidence-support estimate, not search similarity.
When sources give different values for the same field, cite all supporting chunks
and explain both values with their source file and page/section in notes.
If an addendum explicitly changes that field and its order is established, use
the latest valid updated value in value and explain the original value and change
in notes. An explicit statement that an addendum changes the deadline establishes
precedence over a differing portal listing; a timezone discrepancy does not undo
that explicit change. Preserve the addendum's written time zone without conversion.
Unrelated addendums do not override the field. Search rank or similarity
does not establish precedence. Do not invent an earlier value absent from evidence.
If precedence is unclear, use value=null, cite the conflicting evidence, set
confidence=0, and explain both values and the unresolved conflict in notes.
Null with citations means unresolved conflict; null without citations means missing.
Preserve stated dates, time zones and relative windows; do not invent details.
A bidder question is not an official requirement: use the official Answer when present.
Never infer "not required" from equipment having an operating system already installed.
Preserve who each rule applies to: district, prime vendor, subcontractor or supplier.
Multiple permitted options or cooperative arrangements are not conflicting values;
list all supported options and explain whether participation is optional.
Keep device categories separate. Do not transfer specifications from one category to another.
Use a heading_context only to identify a passage's category; it supplies no missing specifications.
Do not assume a warranty, operating system, quantity or other unstated value.
For broad fields, enumerate all categories supported by the supplied evidence and
explicitly identify incomplete coverage. Do not turn a subset into an all-devices claim.
If a fixed delivery date is absent but scheduling or a relative window is supported,
report that information and say the fixed date is not established.
Table evidence with table_complete=false is partial; do not claim a complete list.

Requested fields:
- Contract or Cooperative to use: Referenced state contract or cooperative vehicle.
- Model_no: Requested product model numbers; distinguish them from part/SKU numbers.
- Part_no: Requested part/SKU numbers; do not invent them from model numbers.

input.content:
Return exactly one JSON entry per requested field,
using only retrieved evidence. Each entry has name, value, source_chunk_ids,
confidence and notes. Values are text or null. A non-null value requires exact
retrieved chunk IDs. Missing fields use null, [], 0 and notes='Not found in
retrieved evidence'. Missing retrieval does not prove absence from the documents.
Explicit negative requirements may be reported as text; absence alone is not 'No'.
Confidence is an uncalibrated evidence-support estimate, not search similarity.
When sources give different values for the same field, cite all supporting chunks
and explain both values with their source file and page/section in notes.
If an addendum explicitly changes that field and its order is established, use
the latest valid updated value in value and explain the original value and change
in notes. An explicit statement that an addendum changes the deadline establishes
precedence over a differing portal listing; a timezone discrepancy does not undo
that explicit change. Preserve the addendum's written time zone without conversion.
Unrelated addendums do not override the field. Search rank or similarity
does not establish precedence. Do not invent an earlier value absent from evidence.
If precedence is unclear, use value=null, cite the conflicting evidence, set
confidence=0, and explain both values and the unresolved conflict in notes.
Null with citations means unresolved conflict; null without citations means missing.
Preserve stated dates, time zones and relative windows; do not invent details.
A bidder question is not an official requirement: use the official Answer when present.
Never infer "not required" from equipment having an operating system already installed.
Preserve who each rule applies to: district, prime vendor, subcontractor or supplier.
Multiple permitted options or cooperative arrangements are not conflicting values;
list all supported options and explain whether participation is optional.
Keep device categories separate. Do not transfer specifications from one category to another.
Use a heading_context only to identify a passage's category; it supplies no missing specifications.
Do not assume a warranty, operating system, quantity or other unstated value.
For broad fields, enumerate all categories supported by the supplied evidence and
explicitly identify incomplete coverage. Do not turn a subset into an all-devices claim.
If a fixed delivery date is absent but scheduling or a relative window is supported,
report that information and say the fixed date is not established.
Table evidence with table_complete=false is partial; do not claim a complete list.

Requested fields:
- Product: Product names and associated quantities.

{"headers": [], "rows": [["PURPOSE OF REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)
This Request for Proposal (RFP) will be for student and staff computing devices, including laptops,
desktops, tablet devices, and display monitors. Vendors participating in this Request for Proposal (RFP) may
submit proposals for one, several, or all categories of devices required by the District. Within each category
of device, the District reserves the right to award contracts to a single vendor or multiple vendors.
The specifications listed in this RFP are the minimum hardware requirements for each tier of device required
by Dallas ISD. Vendors responding to this RFP must have the ability to provide the District with significant
quantities of devices as requested in the pricing lines in this RFP. Note that quantities requested by Dallas
ISD are estimates to be ordered over the five years of the contracts resulting from this RFP. Purchases may
also include a variety of device accessories which will be ordered in a bundle along with the devices. Such
accessories include, but are not limited to, sleeves, cases, mice, keyboards, and cables that may not
necessarily come with the devices.
Each submission must include a detailed plan as to how the vendor will track all shipped products and
provide deployment services. Processes and procedures are required in the response, which outlines how
tracking will be executed and any processes for providing white glove services.
The awarded vendors shall provide Dallas ISD with computing devices that meet all current industry
standard specifications. The awarded vendors and Dallas ISD EdTech-Enterprise Support Services shall
meet every six months or as needed to discuss technology advancements related to computing devices to
be selected by Dallas ISD.
Note: For each purchase during the term of the contracts resulting from this RFP, the District will seek
competitive quotes from one or more of the awarded vendors.", null]]}

Example,
for just the Chrome requirement where Dallas is asking for the standard one-year warranty. We
could expand these options for this product alone to: Two year onsite, Two-year ADP (accidental
damage protection), Two year onsite and ADP then three-year, four year and five years.
How would Dallas like us to explain this point? Can Dallas put more boxes in Oracle so we can
have costs per option?
Answer: As a minimum requirement, Dallas ISD is asking for a one-year warranty for
student Chromebooks and three years for student and staff Windows laptops. The
system will only take one input, additional warranty information and pricing can be
submitted as an attachment.
8. Does Dallas prefer for the warranties to be underwritten by insurance? Example: If you pay for
an additional warranty and that company goes under, if your warranty was not underwritten
you would lose your investment. If it were underwritten the warranty would continue as
purchased.

Explicit negative requirements may be reported as text; absence alone is not 'No'.
Confidence is an uncalibrated evidence-support estimate, not search similarity.
When sources give different values for the same field, cite all supporting chunks
and explain both values with their source file and page/section in notes.
If an addendum explicitly changes that field and its order is established, use
the latest valid updated value in value and explain the original value and change
in notes. An explicit statement that an addendum changes the deadline establishes
precedence over a differing portal listing; a timezone discrepancy does not undo
that explicit change. Preserve the addendum's written time zone without conversion.
Unrelated addendums do not override the field. Search rank or similarity
does not establish precedence. Do not invent an earlier value absent from evidence.

confidence=0, and explain both values and the unresolved conflict in notes.
Null with citations means unresolved conflict; null without citations means missing.
Preserve stated dates, time zones and relative windows; do not invent details.
A bidder question is not an official requirement: use the official Answer when present.
Never infer "not required" from equipment having an operating system already installed.
Preserve who each rule applies to: district, prime vendor, subcontractor or supplier.
Multiple permitted options or cooperative arrangements are not conflicting values;
list all supported options and explain whether participation is optional.
Keep device categories separate. Do not transfer specifications from one category to another.

For broad fields, enumerate all categories supported by the supplied evidence and

report that information and say the fixed date is not established.

fields.name: Bid Summary
fields.value: Dallas ISD issued an RFP for student and staff computing devices, including laptops, desktops, tablets, and display monitors, allowing vendors to submit proposals for any or all categories (01da76cd-9c09-5a71-89e6-e818ce0b6d8e). Minimum hardware requirements are defined per tier, such as Tier 1 Small Student Chromebook laptops requiring an Intel Celeron N100 processor, 8 GB DDR5 RAM, 64 GB eMMC storage, an 11.6‑inch display, and a 1‑year warranty (ff50c3b2-00fd-5ab6-9e15-3d40d0402c23). Tier 2 Large Student Chromebooks must have an Intel Celeron N100, 8 GB DDR5 RAM, 128 GB eMMC storage, a 14‑inch non‑touch display, and a 1‑year warranty (241083d7-093d-5230-9562-09dadfbca0d2). Tier 3 Student Windows laptops are required to include an Intel i5 13th‑gen processor, at least 16 GB DDR5 RAM, a 256 GB NVMe SSD, a 13‑inch display, Windows 11 Pro, and a minimum 3‑year warranty (10241926-c045-50af-9194-fda5010f277f; 241083d7-093d-5230-9562-09dadfbca0d2). Staff device tiers include a Tier 1 Basic Desktop with Intel i5 14th‑gen CPU, 16 GB RAM, 512 GB NVMe SSD, a 23.8‑inch touch screen, and a 3‑year warranty; a Tier 2 Professional Desktop with Intel i7 14th‑gen CPU, 32 GB DDR5 RAM, 1 TB NVMe SSD, and a 3‑year warranty; a Tier 1 Basic Laptop with Intel i5 14th‑gen CPU, 16 GB DDR5 RAM, 512 GB SSD, and a 3‑year warranty; and a Tier 2 Staff Laptop with Intel i7 14th‑gen CPU, 32 GB DDR5 RAM, 1 TB SSD, and a 3‑year warranty (953ce287-8b12-51df-ac8e-2e6d136d7b80; 214c74f4-2590-56b2-98a9-139fe8f5d645; 926de634-56ec-5da4-8943-25ab93b516c5). Additional requirements cover staff tablets with an A13 processor, 10.2‑inch Retina display, 64 GB storage, iOS 17, and a 1‑year warranty, as well as 24‑inch touch and non‑touch display monitors with 1920 × 1080 resolution and a 3‑year warranty (10241926-c045-50af-9194-fda5010f277f; 214c74f4-2590-56b2-98a9-139fe8f5d645).

fields.name: Product Specification
fields.value: Tier 1 Small Student Chromebook Laptop: Intel Celeron N100 (or equivalent) CPU, 8 GB DDR5 RAM, 64 GB eMMC storage, 11.6‑inch diagonal display (1366 × 768 multi‑touch), 720p camera, Wi‑Fi 6E (802.11AX) and Bluetooth 5.1, Type‑C 65 W power, 10‑hour battery, Chrome OS license required, 1‑year warranty (ff50c3b2-00fd-5ab6-9e15-3d40d0402c23). Tier 2 Large Student Chromebook Laptop: Intel Celeron N100 CPU, 8 GB DDR5 RAM, 128 GB eMMC storage, 14‑inch non‑touch display (1920 × 1080), 720p camera, Wi‑Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.1, Type‑C 65 W, 10‑hour battery, Chrome OS license, 1‑year warranty (241083d7-093d-5230-9562-09dadfbca0d2). Tier 3 Student Windows Laptop: Intel i5 13th‑gen CPU, 16 GB DDR5 RAM (minimum), 256 GB NVMe SSD, 13‑inch diagonal display (1920 × 1080 non‑touch), 720p camera, Wi‑Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.1, Type‑C 65 W, 10‑hour battery, Windows 11 Pro, 3‑year warranty (10241926-c045-50af-9194-fda5010f277f; 241083d7-093d-5230-9562-09dadfbca0d2). Student Tablet: Apple A13 processor, 10.2‑inch Retina display, 8 MP wide camera, 2160 × 1620 multi‑touch resolution, 64 GB storage, iOS 17, Wi‑Fi 5 (802.11ac) and Bluetooth 4.2, 10‑hour battery, 1‑year warranty (10241926-c045-50af-9194-fda5010f277f). Tier 1 Staff Windows Basic Desktop: Intel i5 14th‑gen CPU, 16 GB RAM, 512 GB NVMe SSD, 23.8‑inch touch screen, Wi‑Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.1, multiple USB/HDMI ports, Windows 11 Pro, 3‑year warranty (953ce287-8b12-51df-ac8e-2e6d136d7b80). Tier 2 Staff Professional Desktop: Intel i7 14th‑gen CPU, 32 GB DDR5 RAM, 1 TB NVMe SSD, 23.8‑inch touch screen, Windows 11 Pro or macOS, Wi‑Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.1, 3‑year warranty (953ce287-8b12-51df-ac8e-2e6d136d7b80). Tier 1 Staff Basic Laptop: Intel i5 14th‑gen CPU, 16 GB DDR5 RAM, 512 GB NVMe SSD, 13‑inch display, 1080p camera, Wi‑Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.1, Type‑C 65 W, 10‑hour battery, Windows 11 or macOS, 3‑year warranty (926de634-56ec-5da4-8943-25ab93b516c5). Tier 2 Staff Laptop: Intel i7 14th‑gen CPU, 32 GB DDR5 RAM, 1 TB NVMe SSD, 13‑inch display, 1080p camera, 1920 × 1080 resolution, Wi‑Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.1, Type‑C 65 W, 10‑hour battery, Windows 11 or macOS, 3‑year warranty (214c74f4-2590-56b2-98a9-139fe8f5d645). Display Monitors (Touch and Non‑Touch): 24‑inch diagonal, 1920 × 1080 resolution, USB 3.1 hub port, 16:9 aspect ratio, 3000:1 contrast, 3‑year warranty (214c74f4-2590-56b2-98a9-139fe8f5d645).

Return exactly one JSON entry per requested field,
using only retrieved evidence. Each entry has name, value, source_chunk_ids,
confidence and notes. Values are text or null. A non-null value requires exact
retrieved chunk IDs. Missing fields use null, [], 0 and notes='Not found in
retrieved evidence'. Missing retrieval does not prove absence from the documents.
Explicit negative requirements may be reported as text; absence alone is not 'No'.
Confidence is an uncalibrated evidence-support estimate, not search similarity.
When sources give different values for the same field, cite all supporting chunks
and explain both values with their source file and page/section in notes.
If an addendum explicitly changes that field and its order is established, use
the latest valid updated value in value and explain the original value and change
in notes. An explicit statement that an addendum changes the deadline establishes
precedence over a differing portal listing; a timezone discrepancy does not undo
that explicit change. Preserve the addendum's written time zone without conversion.
Unrelated addendums do not override the field. Search rank or similarity
does not establish precedence. Do not invent an earlier value absent from evidence.
If precedence is unclear, use value=null, cite the conflicting evidence, set
confidence=0, and explain both values and the unresolved conflict in notes.
Null with citations means unresolved conflict; null without citations means missing.
Preserve stated dates, time zones and relative windows; do not invent details.
A bidder question is not an official requirement: use the official Answer when present.
Never infer "not required" from equipment having an operating system already installed.
Preserve who each rule applies to: district, prime vendor, subcontractor or supplier.
Multiple permitted options or cooperative arrangements are not conflicting values;
list all supported options and explain whether participation is optional.
Keep device categories separate. Do not transfer specifications from one category to another.
Use a heading_context only to identify a passage's category; it supplies no missing specifications.
Do not assume a warranty, operating system, quantity or other unstated value.
For broad fields, enumerate all categories supported by the supplied evidence and
explicitly identify incomplete coverage. Do not turn a subset into an all-devices claim.
If a fixed delivery date is absent but scheduling or a relative window is supported,
report that information and say the fixed date is not established.
Table evidence with table_complete=false is partial; do not claim a complete list.

fields.name: Bid Summary
fields.value: The RFP seeks student and staff computing devices—including laptops, desktops, tablets, and display monitors—and allows vendors to submit proposals for any or all categories, with the District able to award contracts to one or multiple vendors. Minimum hardware tiers are defined, such as Tier 1 Small Student Chromebook laptops requiring 64 GB eMMC storage, a Chrome OS license and a 1‑year warranty; Tier 2 Large Student Chromebooks requiring 128 GB eMMC, 8 GB DDR5 memory, Wi‑Fi 6E, and a 1‑year warranty; and Tier 3 Student Windows laptops requiring Autopilot‑ready management, an Intel i5 13th‑Gen processor, and Windows 11 Pro. Staff device tiers include Tier 1 Staff Windows Basic Desktops with an Intel i5 14th‑Gen processor, 16 GB RAM, 512 GB NVMe SSD, Windows 11 Pro and a 3‑year warranty; Tier 2 Staff Professional Desktops with an Intel i7 14th‑Gen processor, 32 GB DDR5 RAM, 1 TB NVMe SSD, and either Windows 11 Pro or macOS, also with a 3‑year warranty. Tier 2 Staff Laptops must be enterprise‑management ready, feature an Intel i7 14th‑Gen CPU, 32 GB DDR5 RAM, 1 TB NVMe SSD, Windows 11 or macOS, and a 3‑year warranty. The RFP also specifies a Student Tablet with an A13 processor, 10.2‑inch Retina display, iOS 17, 64 GB storage and a 1‑year warranty, and display monitors (both touch and non‑touch) with a minimum 24‑inch screen, 1920 × 1080 resolution, USB 3.1 hub and a 3‑year warranty.
fields.notes: Summary excludes any staff tablet specifications, as the evidence only provides a Student Tablet requirement (chunk 10241926). All statements are directly supported by the cited chunks.
